messages.subject: Re: Hyperfire Metadata Fix not working
parts:
Hi Elsa,
my apologies for the late reply. The error you encountered

Error in isTRUE(returnFileNamesMissingTags) : 
  argument "returnFileNamesMissingTags" is missing, with no default

is a bug in the current release of camtrapR and will be fixed in the next version coming soon (there is other threads in the group discussing it).

The other issue is more puzzling:
Warning: CamtrapRData:   metadataSpeciesTag 'Species' not found in image metadata tag 'HierarchicalSubject'.

It is puzzling because the tag tree looks fine to me. Can you share the output of exifTagNames with argument returnMetadata = TRUE? Please make sure that the image the function returns metadata for has a species tag. In addition, can you please also share a tagged picture? It may help find what causes camtrapR not to recognise the tags.

Thank you,
Jürgen

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: Hyperfire Metadata Fix not working
parts:
Hi Elsa,
did you rename the tag groups in digiKam? In the metadata I see the relevant species tag as:

06Species|Chiroptera sp.

So when you run any function that extracts metadata the following will not work:
metadataSpeciesTag         = "Species" 

The following should work:
metadataSpeciesTag         = "06Species"

Unfortunately I cannot test with the attached picture, as the metadata were removed during upload (likely a Google Group issue).

So maybe you renamed the tag group and did not update the tags in the images? The relevant button is called "Write metadata to each file"? For some more info on this see the vignette. Adding the group as a tag then maybe updated the whole hierarchical metadata and it then worked. Other than that there is no need to add the group ("Species") as a tag. In fact you can see the empty "Species" tag from assigning the group highlighted in red as a tag separately from the actual species tag in the metadata you shared in blue:

[50] "[XMP]           Hierarchical Subject            : 06Species, 09Sex|unknown, 11Direction|right, 02Site|Terk02, 05Category|wildlife, 03Camera|RHC06, 06Species|Chiroptera sp., 10Age|adult, 07NBIndividuals|1, 12IDedIndividual, 08Behaviour|swimmimg, 12IDedIndividual|shyena1, 01Survey|Terkei 2019, 04Setup|single"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          


If you didn't rename the tag group I don't know why this would happen.
Best,
Jürgen
